key_insight: The paper shows that an LLM can carry out end-to-end autonomous research in computational physics when every stage is grounded in literature, reproduced benchmarks, and fault-tolerant multi-session execution.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical blueprint for building reliable AI research agents in high-stakes scientific domains where correctness must be anchored by external evidence rather than internal model priors.
method: Mapped 11,083 recent condensed-matter arXiv papers to identify and choose a research direction.
Used fresh-context, multi-phase sessions with shared on-disk state to reproduce published results before running new first-principles calculations.
Applied adversarial review and literature consultation to catch errors and enforce numerical confrontation at calibration checkpoints.
evidence_signal: The pipeline was evaluated across 47 fresh-context sessions in six phases, with 2,162 literature-consultation events and a manuscript containing three substantive physics findings.
watch_item: The approach still depends on bounded human intervention when reproduction fails, so full autonomy is not yet guaranteed in all cases.
paper_title: Grounded autonomous research: a fault-tolerant LLM pipeline from corpus to manuscript in frontier computational physics
